title: Coat a PVC pipe band and fitting socket, leaving no bare window or cement on the stop or in either bore
instruction: Coat the pipe all round down to the line, then the socket wall, then the pipe all round again after a fresh dip. Keep cement off the stop and out of both bores. Put the dauber back and let go.
context: Plumbers and pipefitters coat PVC pipe and fitting sockets before solvent joining (O*NET 47-2152.00; BLS: 510,600 jobs in 2025). Oatey Rain-R-Shine directions call for pipe, socket, then a second pipe coat. This task tests that coating step and protection of the bore; it does not join or test a joint.
setup: Millimetres; x away from the arms, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. A plumber's bench with two small cast-iron bench vises (base 120 x 100 x 15, jaws 70 x 18; sizes estimated), both fixed. Vise 1 holds upright a 100 mm offcut of 1-1/2 in Schedule 40 PVC pipe (Charlotte Pipe; OD 48.26, minimum wall 3.68), axis at (290, -220), top end 115 above the bench, jaw tops 68; a black line is drawn round it 18.3 below the top (the socket depth). Vise 2 holds a 1-1/2 in pipe stub with a Charlotte PVC DWV coupling, part no. 100 (hub x hub, model length 39.775, catalogue centre stop 3.175; socket mouth 48.6, depth 18.3 and outside 56 obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026)) pushed dry onto it: axis at (200, -100), open mouth 105 above the bench, stop face 86.7. An Oatey Rain-R-Shine medium blue PVC cement can, 8 fl oz (item 30891; round, 70 across, 87 to the shoulder, neck 36 across up to 95; chosen surface 40 above the can bottom; 0.25 kg; sizes estimated), stands at (180, -270) with its lid dauber resting loose on the neck: blue lid 40 across x 16, 2.5 mm wire 45 long, wool swab 19 across (obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product, Nov 2026) x 25 long (length estimated), 12 g, the swab hanging in the cement. Lot B moves the can with its dauber to (245, -345). Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 for actual wet-wool contact depositing blue on the coupling stop, inside either bore, or on the bench outside the can; or if the can tips more than 15 degrees or slides more than 20 mm. Real grading: photographs within 30 s, a torch and mirror for stop/bores, and overhead/wrist video for gross order and can movement. Divide each surface into 6 rows x 48 columns (about 3.0 x 3.2 mm); a window counts when blue is visible in it. Simulation: actual reported wool contact totaling at least 0.20 N on that surface, window under the wool and within 6 mm of contact around the circumference; 3,200 mm2 coating budget per dip, estimates. No hidden squeeze depth or socket re-coat penalty. Every nonzero score requires the dauber and can at rest and both hands at least 30 mm away for the final 1 s. 1.0: all windows of both surfaces coated; one full pipe orbit before first socket entry, another after final exit and a fresh dip; dauber back in can, lid within 3 mm vertically/6 mm horizontally/10 degrees upright. Real graders count the two full turns in contact on video; the simulator also requires every pipe window in each pass. 0.75: all windows of both surfaces coated without satisfying the full-score order/stow conditions. 0.5: one surface complete and at least half of the other. 0.25: one surface complete. 0 otherwise. Average lots A and B.
run_limit: 2,400 steps per layout (120 seconds at 20 Hz); two fixed layouts, A then B.
reset_notes: 1. Clamp a new 100 mm offcut of 1-1/2 in Schedule 40 PVC (cut in advance) upright in vise 1, standing on the vise base, top 115 mm above the bench, axis (290, -220); draw a line round it 18.3 mm below the top. 2. Push a new Charlotte no. 100 coupling by hand onto the pipe stub in vise 2 (dry, no cement), mouth 105 mm above the bench, axis (200, -100). 3. Stir the cement and set its surface 40 mm above the can bottom (scene choice), stand the can at (180, -270) (lot B: (245, -345)) and rest the lid dauber loose on the neck with the swab in the cement. 4. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open; start within 15 s. About a minute per reset; nothing cures. Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection, ventilate, no ignition sources.
fidelity: Dry 19 mm dauber resistance ~40 g/mm; socket mouth/depth/OD 48.6/18.3/56 mm, obtained by phone from a technician who works with this product (Nov 2026). Colliding wool: 392.266 N/m per contact (earlier 200 N/m press: 0.3-0.45 N at 0.9 mm). Wet friction .20/.15, transfer >=.20 N and 3,200 mm2/dip estimated. Physical reaction on held tool/fixed vises. Straight socket; can/lid/wire/wool length estimated. No fluid/cure/bond; no upper-force penalty. One arm operates.
scores: Revised contact model, runs demo-20261124T034740 and dream-20261124T035644: scripted demo A/B 1.0/1.0; Dream-1 A/B 0.0/0.0 (both lots reached the 2,400-step limit).
